claims.text: Schema evolution: changing the shape of data that other programs read, such as a message body, while those programs keep running.

DonHang.Domain.OrderMessage, DonHang.Notifications.OrderMessage and DonHang.Payments.OrderMessage are separate records with the same four properties (OrderId, CustomerEmail, CustomerName, OccurredAt); the services share no class.

claims.text: By default System.Text.Json skips JSON properties that match no member or constructor parameter of the target type (JsonUnmappedMemberHandling.Skip); JsonSerializerOptions.Web does not change this.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs, System.Text.Json: Handle unmapped members / JsonUnmappedMemberHandling

claims.text: When a constructor parameter of a record has no matching JSON property, System.Text.Json passes its default value (null for a string) unless RespectRequiredConstructorParameters is on; JsonSerializerOptions.Web leaves it off.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs, System.Text.Json: immutable types / parameterized constructors; JsonSerializerOptions.RespectRequiredConstructorParameters

claims.text: OrderEventsConsumer.Read deserialises with JsonSerializerOptions.Web and throws PoisonMessageException when the result is null, OrderId < 1 or CustomerEmail is null or empty; RefundRequestedConsumer has the same check.

On PoisonMessageException the consumer calls BasicRejectAsync with requeue: false; the quorum queue notifications.order-events then dead-letters the message via notifications.dead-letter to notifications.order-events.dead.

RabbitMQ records why a message was dead-lettered in the x-first-death-reason header; a message rejected with requeue false has the reason rejected.

claims.text: A deploy does not remove unsent outbox rows or messages in the durable queues; the relay sends the rows and the queue delivers its messages after the deploy, in the shape they were written with.

claims.text: Nothing moves a dead-lettered message back automatically; it is delivered again only when a person moves it back.

claims.text: OrderMessageContractTests serialises the api's OrderMessage (JsonSerializerOptions.Web), reads it with both copies and asserts the four values arrive. A rename or retype on either side fails it; a reader newly requiring a property does not: only the current shape is sent.

notifications.order-events is bound to the topic exchange donhang.orders with order.*, where * matches exactly one word, so a routing key with one word after order. reaches the queue and one with two words after order. does not.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.Notifications/RabbitMqTopology.cs @ stage-4 (QueueBindAsync order.*); RabbitMQ docs, Topic exchange

claims.text: OrderEventsConsumer.SubjectFor maps a routing key to an email subject and throws PoisonMessageException for a routing key outside its table (order.placed, order.cancelled, order.shipped, order.refund-requested, order.refunded, order.refund-failed).

Trade-offs: adding an optional property is safe in one release; rename/remove/retype in place: readers reject (poison), redeliver to the delivery limit if a later step fails, or misread; newly requiring a property breaks old messages; a new routing key outside old bindings costs double publishing.
claims.source_hint: Outline items 3-5; claims 4-6, 19; JsonSerializerOptions.Web NumberHandling = AllowReadingFromString

claims.text: An added property optional in the reader lets the api or Notifications release first; make it required only when no message without it is left anywhere. A type change cannot be added beside itself, so it goes under a new routing key.
A rename that only tidies a name is not worth a message migration when every reader, queued message and the test already agree on the old name.
Adding ShopId to the api's OrderMessage only leaves both Read*EveryValueTheApiSends tests passing: each copy skips shopId and the assertions compare only the four shared values.

A body without customerName passes Read, but Notifications saves FullName into the NOT NULL full_name column; the save fails, the message is requeued, and the quorum queue dead-letters it once x-delivery-limit (5) is exceeded.
